title: True-scale system view (1/4): remove the miniature orrery, render the star as a distant sun
description: SCALE DECISION (human-approved 2026-10-06): the game is 1 u = 1 m everywhere and the RENDERED world must match the SIM world. Today it does not. The in-system view draws the whole system as a ~130 m miniature model around the spawn — `buildWorldGroup` / `buildSystemLayout` in src/client/world/WorldManager.ts (~lines 60-245): a 14 m star sphere at the origin (WORLD_STAR_RADIUS) and WORLD_PLANET_COUNT = 2 planets of radius 4 m (WORLD_PLANET_RADIUS) on 30-48 m orbits. None of it exists in the sim: sim planets are 1 km atmosphere bubbles on the y = 0 plane at `planetAnchor(i)` = ((i + 1) × 10 000, 0, 0) (src/shared/galaxy/planets.ts). A ship at 120 m/s flies through the whole miniature 'system' in about a second, which is why players report that the ships cross the system in seconds. This task removes the miniature model and replaces the 14 m star ball with a SUN rendered like the skybox (infinitely far, fixed direction). TASK-83 then draws the planets where the sim has them; TASK-84 mounts the terrain; TASK-85 adds a space cruise boost.

steps.details: New `src/client/render/sun.ts`. Export `SUN_DIRECTION` = normalize(-1, 0.12, 0) — the sim star is at the origin and every planet anchor lies along +X, so from anywhere in the system the star is toward −X (the spawn gate at (100, 0, 0) faces −X: SPAWN_GATE_QUAT in src/shared/galaxy/spawn.ts — a warped-in ship looks straight at the sun); the small +Y keeps it above the y = 0 horizon. Export `SUN_DISTANCE = 380` (inside the 420 m sky shell so it draws over the sky, TASK-75 keeps both camera-centred) and `SUN_ANGULAR_RADIUS_DEG = 2`. Export a pure `sunPosition(cameraPos: Vec3): Vec3` = cameraPos + SUN_DIRECTION × SUN_DISTANCE. Unit test (`sun.test.ts`): direction is unit length, points to −X with positive y; sunPosition is camera-relative (moving the camera by D moves the sun by exactly D).

In sun.ts export `createSun(color: string): { mesh: THREE.Mesh; setOpacity(o: number): void; dispose(): void }`: a small sphere (radius = SUN_DISTANCE × tan(SUN_ANGULAR_RADIUS_DEG)) with MeshBasicMaterial in the star color (STAR_COLORS[system.star.class] — keep STAR_COLORS where it is in WorldManager.ts or move it next to the sun, your call), `transparent: true`, `depthWrite: false`, `fog: false`, renderOrder 1.5 is not allowed (integers only) — use renderOrder 1 like the stars and add it to the scene AFTER the stars so it draws over them. A soft glow is optional (a second, larger sphere at low opacity) — keep it cheap: at most 2 draw calls.

steps.description: Wire the sun into WorldManager; delete the orrery
steps.details: In WorldManager: create the sun in the constructor, add it to the scene, and every frame — right where TASK-75 anchors the background to the camera (immediately before render) — set `sun.mesh.position` from `sunPosition(camera.position)`. Re-tint on `swapWorld` (new system → new star class color). In `setAtmosphereView` scale the sun's opacity by the same `fade` as the stars (inside a thick atmosphere the sun fades with the sky — the one-number no-desync contract of TASK-28.1). Point the existing DirectionalLight `keyLight` along SUN_DIRECTION (keyLight.position = SUN_DIRECTION) so the ship is lit from the sun. In `buildWorldGroup` DELETE the star sphere and the planet spheres; keep the spawn gate torus (it is already sim-scale: 100 m from the origin) and the pad rings / hazard discs. Remove `buildSystemLayout`'s planet/orbit layout and the now-unused WORLD_STAR_RADIUS / WORLD_PLANET_RADIUS / WORLD_FIRST_ORBIT / WORLD_ORBIT_STEP / WORLD_PLANET_COUNT / PLANET_COLORS exports IF nothing else imports them (grep first — PLANET_COLORS will be needed again by TASK-83: keep it). Update `world-manager.test.ts` (and any other test asserting the orrery) to the new layout — change expectations, do not delete coverage of the gate/pads.

steps.description: Onboarding text points at the nav marker, not the star
steps.details: `src/client/ui/guidance.ts` (~line 28) step 1 reads 'Hold W to fly toward the star. Press M for the star chart.' — flying toward the star now flies AWAY from every planet. Change it to e.g. 'Hold W to fly. Steer with A/D and R/F to follow the nav marker to the planet. Press M for the star chart.' and update `guidance-hint.test.tsx`. Keep it one line in the HUD.

Update any e2e that asserted the star sphere at the canvas centre (grep tests/e2e for `canvasCenterLuminanceMean`, 'star', 'orrery': e.g. warp.spec.ts TASK-8 asserts a bright canvas centre after warp because the star sat at the origin — after warp the ship faces −X = the sun, so the sun is near the centre: re-point the assertion at the sun's projected position via a dev probe if needed). Add to an existing in-system spec: the sun's projected screen position after a fresh warp is inside the viewport and the sampled 8×8 region there is bright (> 150 mean). Screenshots `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-82-1.png` (spawn: sun visible, no miniature planets/star ball) — LOOK at it. Then `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit`, full `npm run test`, e2e: warp, core-flow, self-ship, flight, deep-space, atmosphere-view, star-chart, first-launch; `npm run bench:render` gates still green; `eslint --fix` + `prettier --write`. Commit `feat(TASK-82): ...`.

acceptanceCriteria: No miniature star/planet meshes remain in the in-system view; the spawn gate, pad rings and hazard discs are unchanged

The star renders as a camera-anchored sun toward −X (slightly above the horizon), tinted by the system's spectral class, faded with the sky inside an atmosphere, and the ship key light comes from the sun direction
Onboarding step 1 no longer tells the player to fly toward the star
Unit tests for sun placement; e2e asserts the sun is on screen after warp; screenshot TASK-82-1 shows the sun and no orrery
`npx tsc --noEmit` green; full `npm run test` green; `npm run bench:render` green; touched e2e specs green; one commit
notes: Scale contract for TASK-82..85: 1 u = 1 m. The SIM is the source of truth (planet anchors, atmosphere radius, pads, deposits, hazards, terrain heights). Rendering must follow it; never move sim positions to fit a visual.
The star chart / galaxy map (src/client/ui chart) is a separate 2D/abstract view — leave it alone.
Do NOT commit the pre-existing dirty `.ralph/screenshots/*.png` mods.
